record.context_brief: Geometric characterization of inner product spaces
record.original_question: Let E be a normed linear space such that for each x ∈ E with ||x|| = 1, one has inf_{||y|| = 1} max{||x + y||, ||x − y||} = √2. Must E be linearly isometric to an inner product space?

evidence.quote: Let E be a normed linear space such that for each x∈E, ||x||=1, we have inf_{||y||=1} max{||x+y||, ||x−y||}=√2. Is then E linearly isometric with an inner product space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a real normed linear space with norm $\|\cdot\|$. Suppose that for every $x \in E$ with $\|x\| = 1$,
$$\inf_{\substack{y \in E \\ \|y\| = 1}} \max\bigl\{\|x + y\|,\ \|x - y\|\bigr\} = \sqrt{2}.$$
Must $E$ be linearly isometric to an inner product space (i.e., must the norm of $E$ be induced by an inner product)?
artifact.category_tag: Geometric characterizations of inner product spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a definitive resolution of this specific characterization problem. The problem fits into the well-known program (going back to Jordan–von Neumann and surveyed by Amir, Senechalle, and others) of finding geometric conditions on a normed space that force it to be an inner product space, but no explicit solved/open status for this exact infimum-of-max condition was located.

status_evidence.title: A Characterization of Inner Product Spaces (Senechalle)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical paper providing a geometric characterization of inner product spaces among normed linear spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The problem belongs to the well-studied area of geometric characterizations of inner product spaces, but no resolution of this exact condition was found.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of inner product spaces via norming vectors (arXiv:2409.12857)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on characterizing inner product spaces among normed spaces via geometric/norming-vector conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to add new characterizations, but no entry matching this particular infimum condition was identified.
